evidence_ladder.purpose: Per-building 90% CI width by power-evidence tier -- the estimator's claim that uncertainty tracks evidence, measured rather than asserted.

2.label: stated critical load (EMPTY -- no per-building disclosure exists)
2.note: No Prince William data-center building publishes a stated critical IT load recoverable from public records (METHODOLOGY 28).

evidence_ladder.headline: Permit-observed buildings (tier 1, n=45) carry a median 90% interval of +/-26.0%, versus +/-60.0% for generic floor-area buildings (tier 4, n=141) -- a 2.3x wider interval for the same modelling effort, purely from the evidence available. Tier 2 (stated critical load) is EMPTY: no building discloses one.

peak_day.basis: ICPRB Prince William peak-day WUP 3,060 vs annual-average 309 gal/MW/day
peak_day.why_it_matters: Utilities size infrastructure to peak day, not annual mean, and the peak coincides with the July-August streamflow minimum (METHODOLOGY 31). The annual-average framing understates the infrastructure-relevant draw by ~10x.
